turns.doctor_question: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me?
turns.patient_response: Hi, thank you. Um, I came in today because I keep having these evenings where I just eat a really large amount of food. I'll buy a whole family-size takeout order, and then I usually add chips or bakery things from the grocery store. And I end up eating most of it myself. It's like I don't even really register how much is gone until I've already eaten it all.

symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly states they have evenings where they eat an unusually large amount of food, such as a family-size takeout order plus chips and bakery items by themselves.

turns.doctor_question: After one of these episodes where you eat a large amount, do you ever try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting the next day, or exercising a lot more than usual?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't do anything like that. I don't make myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives or anything. I don't really exercise much to begin with, so I definitely don't do that to make up for it. And I don't skip meals the next day either. I just... I just eat it and that's it.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly denies engaging in non-purging compensatory behaviors such as excessive exercise or skipping meals after eating.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies engaging in purging behaviors, stating they do not make themselves throw up or take laxatives.

turns.doctor_question: During these episodes, do you feel a sense of being out of control—like you can't stop eating even if you want to—and do you feel upset, guilty, or distressed about it afterward?
turns.patient_response: Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start, there is this awful switch that flips. I can actually be thinking to myself, Taylor, put it away, but my hands just keep opening containers anyway. It's like I am not the one in charge. And then afterward... yes, I feel incredibly guilty and upset about the whole thing.

symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly confirms feeling a complete lack of control over eating once started, feeling as though they are not the one in charge.
symptom_reasoning.S055: The patient explicitly affirms feeling incredibly guilty and upset afterward following the eating episodes.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past three months, about how many times per week have you had these large binge-eating episodes?
turns.patient_response: Um, well, I actually keep a journal. And when I look back through it, there has barely been a single week in the last several months without at least one of these nights. Honestly, most weeks, it happens several times.
